in patients with non–smal cell lung carcinoma, COX-2 and PGE2 are involved in the regulation of lymphocyte proliferation, IL-10/INF-γ and T-bet/GATA-3 expression.
COX-2 and PGE2 play a pivotal role in regulating lymphocyte functions and immune dysfunction in NSCLC.

In summary, our research is concerned with
the molecular mechanism of COX-2-mediated immunosuppression in NSCLC.
the molecular mechanism underlying the COX-2-mediated regulation of IL-10 production in NSCLC.
elucidation of the mechanism involved in CO2-mediated immunosuppression in NSCLC.

the COX-2/PGE2–mediated IL-10 production and the subsequent immunosuppression in NSCLC is due to the defect in T-bet and/or GATA-3 expression, which are regulated by ERK and P38 pathways in cooperation with the COX- 2 pathway.
